## 🏛️ Business Context
Macroeconomic stability is the backdrop for all business planning. Banks, insurance companies, and government agencies rely on forecasts of **Inflation** and **Economic Growth** to set interest rates, pricing, and policy. This track focuses on the "Big Picture" of the economy.

## 📊 The Data
You will use the **FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data)** database, the gold standard for economic research.
- **Source**: [FRED API or Database](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/)
- **Target Series**: Consumer Price Index (CPI `CPIAUCSL`) or Unemployment Rate (`UNRATE`).

## 🛠️ Technical Requirements
In addition to the core project requirements, your analysis must address:
1.  **Unit Roots & Differencing**: Economic series are notoriously non-stationary. You must use **ADF tests** and interpret the "Integration" order ($d$) carefully.
2.  **Leading Indicators**: Can the "Yield Curve" (Spread between 10yr and 2yr bonds) predict future unemployment? Try to find a **Leading Indicator** in FRED to use as a regressor.
3.  **Low Frequency High Stakes**: Economic data is often monthly or quarterly. This means "Sample Size" is small ($N < 500$), making model over-fitting a major risk.

## 📑 Professional References
- [fpppy: Stationarity and Differencing](https://otexts.com/fpppy/nbs/09-arima.html#stationarity-and-differencing)
- [FRED St. Louis: Guide to Economic Data](https://fredhelp.stlouisfed.org/)

::: {.businessbox}
**Industry Insight**: The "Consensus Forecast" is a simple average of many different bank models. Often, being "Directionally Correct" on a major economic shift is more valuable than having a lower RMSE during stable times.
:::
